comments.text:
The RX 6400 is objectively the better choice if you focus on frametimes and your 1% low's aswell as 0.1% low's. AMD also has a more matured driver for the RX 6400 and offers more features (AFMF 2, RSR, RIS, Anti-Lag, FreeSync, Radeon Chill, Radeon Boost, etc) that can be used to further improve your gaming experience and make this purchase last you longer. For the overall considerably small price difference (you can look into getting a used RX 6400 if the price difference bothers you that much), it's a very good investment considering the matured and more performant RX 6400 drivers, the features that it provides (hell, it can even do raytracing with acceptable FPS if you tinker with the settings and resolution, AFMF 2 could give you more FPS) and the sheer quality that AMD provides over Intel in the GPU market (AMD has been in the dedicated GPU market longer than Intel, and has been a really good competitor against Nvidia), I would judge it quite a bad financial move to get the ARC A310 over the RX 6400, a bad financial move that could hurt you bad in the longterm. 

TL;DR: Get the RX 6400, the price gap is worth it.
comments.author: @rayzorum2295

comments.text:
Also, why are you using a 13th gen i7 🤣🤣🤣
(Common mistake I see with people getting budget gaming GPUs is that they also get extremely old CPUs. Sure, something like a 4th gen i5 will work well on older games or less-demanding games, it'll become apparent that you'll run into serious CPU bottlenecking with more intensive games or CPU-intensive games. For the RX 6400, I'd pair it with an i3 12100F. It is a 12th gen, taking advantage of the Alder Lake architecture, but it's the weakest of the Alder Lake 12th gen architecture, making it a perfect combo with the RX 6400.)

You're thinking of budget in a short-term manner. Sure, buying a PS5 would provide more performance for less money, but that is if you're not counting the online subscription you have to constantly pay for to be able to play online on paid games, the limited OS that doesn't let you customize to your heart's content and the inaccessibility to online game stores. Furthermore, you're limited to a controller. People may prefer playing on a keyboard and mouse, which is a no-go on consoles. To add even more, it's mostly on what people like to have and want to deal with. Cause remember, you're planning to make this system last, you might aswell have a system that you enjoy using. And many people may prefer a PC due to the sheer customisation it provides and liberty it delivers to users and gamers. 

TL;DR: Buying a PS5 is effectively not a bad idea financially, until you think of it in a long-term manner.
